text: The Patriots' 35-6 evisceration at the hands of the Jaguars has ignited a searching conversation about whether New England is deploying Drake Maye effectively, with the quarterback himself taking ownership of what he called an "unacceptable" offensive performance after coughing up two interceptions and a lost fumble in Sunday's blowout. Film breakdowns are dissecting what went wrong for Maye and the offense—both in terms of scheme and execution—while beat writers are raising the uncomfortable question of whether the Patriots' approach to utilizing their young signal-caller is fundamentally sound. Head Coach Mike Vrabel fielded questions about the loss on Monday, and meanwhile the defense had its own issues, as Jacksonville's Lawrence orchestrated a clinical assault with three touchdown passes. One bright spot: Marcus Jones picked off a pass to record his first interception of the season, though it proved a meager consolation in a game that left plenty of soul-searching ahead.
